Finite values far outside the uint8 range should saturate; kernels must avoid converting an out-of-range rounded float to i32 before clamping.
Infinite inputs are valid float tensor values and should saturate to quantized bounds without first converting infinity to i32.
Vec4 zero-point path: infinite inputs should saturate to uint8 bounds without converting infinity to i32 first.

skipGpu.reason: The QuantizeLinear kernels only implement uint8/int8 output clamps; int16 needs round-to-even plus saturation to [-32768, 32767] before the standard route can be enabled.

provenance.notes: Covers the packed bulk plus scalar tail with a scalar zero point.
Covers the packed bulk plus scalar tail without a zero point.

Per-axis scale on the innermost axis with the zero point omitted, so the vec4-bound scale path runs with the implicit zero. Each channel uses a different scale and the first column ties on .5 in both directions, so a lane reading the wrong channel or rounding half-away-from-zero changes the output.
Valid blocked quantization with per-block zero-points on the last axis.
Blocked quantization clamps the scaled value to int32 range before conversion, then applies round-to-even and output saturation.
Blocked quantization with axis -3, block size two and a partial fifth-axis entry checks axis normalization, signed int8 rounding and both saturation bounds.
Negative axis -3, a partial final block, lane-varying signed zero points and saturating inputs distinguish asymmetric blocked quantization from symmetric quantization.
Last-axis quantization with one scale per four values checks negative rounding and signed saturation.
The blocked last-axis vec4 path uses an int8 zero point, checking the signed zero-point read independently of the uint8 form.
Four consecutive values cross a six-element row boundary, so they can require different per-axis scales and zero points.

Symmetric per-channel quantization over six-element rows omits y_zero_point, so it defaults to zero. Four-lane vectors cross row boundaries and may require two scale entries; signed int8 output preserves negative values, and a coprime seven-value cycle gives every row a distinct lane pattern. No quotient lands on a half-way tie.

Exact opset-25 precision witness: with f16 y_scale and omitted precision, x/y_scale is evaluated in f16. The f16 quotient rounds above 13.5 and then rounds to integer 14; an f32 division incorrectly produces 13.
With precision=FLOAT (TensorProto code 1), explicit f32 division produces a quotient that rounds to 13.
Float32 X with a float16 Y scale divides in float16 by default: 35.25 / 2.611328125 rounds to 13.5 and quantizes to 14.
Float16 X with a float32 Y scale divides in float32 by default: 35.25 / 2.611328125 = 13.499 quantizes to 13.

Exact opset-25 precision=FLOAT16 witness with float32 x and y_scale. The division is explicitly evaluated in f16, where the quotient rounds above 13.5 and then rounds to integer 14; ignoring precision and dividing in f32 incorrectly produces 13.

ONNX Runtime's CPU provider truncates the f16 quotient toward zero instead of rounding half-to-even. All four x values and the scale are f16-exact multiples of 2^-15 / 2^-14; the quotients are 0.5003052... and exactly 0.5, so the expected output is the same whether the division is evaluated in f16 or f32.
